rv.q: It's a delightful piece of material centered on the female experience and based on the 2007. Adrienne Shelly movie.
Simply put, “Waitress” is a triumph and immensely enjoyable.
Director and choreographer Katie Spelman gives the audience an evening of laughter, some tears and love.
Paramount Theatre’s production serves up a star-powered, visually delightful experience—the perfect cherry on top.
This confection of a musical is as satisfying and sweet as one of Jenna’s pies, made from sugar…butter…flour…and baked with lots of love.
Go see, and hear, for yourself.
Lauto’s stunning, soul-searching ballad “She Used to Be Mine”—the showstopping highlight of the night.
At its core, Waitress is about heart.
Now comes the Aurora theater's highly entertaining regional premiere of “Waitress,” the warmhearted musical by award-winning composer/lyricist Sara Bareilles and writer Jessie Nelson.
Well, let me tell you what's inside- a wonderful, albeit longer than expected, version of the show that won four Broadway's Tony Awards and will now shake the City of Aurora through the end of March.
Paramount Theatre’s “Waitress” dishes up top-shelf performances, innovative design, and heartfelt storytelling.
